title: Shadowserver reports around 4,200 internet-exposed instances of AI hacking frameworks, per Cyber Security News
date_note: Cyber Security News dates Shadowserver's report to 25 November; the article itself is dated 26 November. The Shadowserver report was not read.
geo_basis: no location stated; exposure is worldwide
summary: Cyber Security News, relaying a Shadowserver report, says Shadowserver found around 4,200 internet-exposed instances of AI hacking frameworks on 23 November 2026. Between 9 and 23 November its honeypots documented more than 10,000 events from over 80 IP addresses, with ARTEX accounting for around 70% of exposed instances on most days. The article says the findings do not show that all 4,200 instances were attacking.
plain: Cyber Security News says Shadowserver found around 4,200 exposed AI hacking tool instances online, mostly ARTEX. It says this does not show that all of them were attacking.
exec: Shadowserver, as relayed by Cyber Security News, found around 4,200 exposed AI hacking tool instances; the article says not all were shown to be attacking.
action: Shadowserver advises limiting access to approved deployments to trusted addresses or a VPN with strong authentication, and isolating and investigating any deployment nobody can verify.

ARTEX accounted for around 70% of exposed instances on most days.

validation.note: Only Cyber Security News was read; Shadowserver's own report could not be found by search and was not read.

review.note: Compared 4,200, 10,000 events, 80 IPs, 70 percent, caveat and advice against Cyber Security News; single_source fits
